title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting
description: Showed that prompting a model with worked, step-by-step examples improves its multi-step reasoning. The idea later became a training target for reasoning models.
capabilityNote: PaLM 540B with 8 chain-of-thought exemplars reached about 57% on GSM8K, versus about 18% with standard prompting.

title: InstructGPT (RLHF for instruction following)
description: Fine-tuned GPT-3 on human demonstrations and then with reinforcement learning from human feedback so it follows instructions. The recipe was the basis for ChatGPT.
capabilityNote: Labelers preferred outputs from the 1.3B InstructGPT model over the 175B GPT-3.

title: Chinchilla (compute-optimal scaling)
description: Found that model size and training tokens should grow roughly in step, and that earlier large language models were undertrained for their size.
capabilityNote: The 70B Chinchilla, trained on 1.4T tokens, outperformed the 280B Gopher.

title: ReAct (reasoning plus acting)
description: Interleaved written reasoning steps with tool actions such as search queries. The loop became the template for most later agent frameworks.
capabilityNote: +34 and +10 points absolute success on ALFWorld and WebShop over imitation and RL baselines.

title: Constitutional AI
description: Trained a model to be harmless using a written list of principles and AI-generated feedback in place of most human harm labels.
capabilityNote: Produced models rated less harmful and less evasive than the RLHF baseline in the paper's evaluations.

title: Sparks of Artificial General Intelligence
description: A qualitative probe of an early GPT-4 build. It was widely cited and also criticized for its non-reproducible method and its AGI framing.
capabilityNote: Anecdotal demonstrations only (drawings, proofs, code); no controlled benchmark.

title: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)
description: Aligned models to human preferences with a simple classification-style loss, removing the separate reward model and RL loop. It became a standard post-training step, especially for open models.
capabilityNote: Matched or beat PPO-based RLHF on summarization and dialogue in the paper's tests.

title: SWE-bench
creators: Carlos Jimenez, John Yang et al.
description: A benchmark of 2,294 real GitHub issues from 12 Python repositories, graded by each repository's own tests. Its 500-task Verified subset (Aug 2024) became the standard yardstick for coding agents.
capabilityNote: At release the best model (Claude 2) solved 1.96%. On the Verified subset, reported scores went from 49% (Oct 2024) to 80.9% (Nov 2025); the two figures are not strictly comparable.

title: Scaling Monosemanticity
description: Applied sparse autoencoders to a production model, Claude 3 Sonnet, and found millions of human-interpretable internal features. It followed a 2023 small-model study and preceded 2025 work tracing circuits.
capabilityNote: Extracted up to 34M features, including abstract, multilingual and safety-relevant ones.

majorUpdates.title: Towards Monosemanticity
majorUpdates.summary: Dictionary learning on a one-layer transformer split neurons into more interpretable features.

majorUpdates.title: Golden Gate Claude
majorUpdates.summary: A public demo that amplified one feature so the model steered every topic toward the Golden Gate Bridge.

majorUpdates.title: Tracing the thoughts of a large language model
majorUpdates.summary: Attribution graphs showed forward planning in rhymes and shared cross-language features in Claude 3.5 Haiku.

title: AlphaFold 3
description: Extended structure prediction from proteins to joint complexes of proteins, DNA, RNA, ligands and ions. Published in Nature.
capabilityNote: At least 50% better than prior methods on protein–molecule interactions (reported).

title: AlphaProof and AlphaGeometry 2 at IMO 2024
description: A reinforcement-learning prover working in the Lean formal language, plus a geometry system, attempted the 2024 olympiad problems. The problems were hand-translated into Lean and some took days to solve.
capabilityNote: 28/42 points, silver-medal level (4 of 6 problems).

majorUpdates.title: AlphaGeometry
majorUpdates.summary: Neuro-symbolic system solved 25 of 30 olympiad geometry problems (gold-medalist average: 25.9).

sources.title: DeepMind: AI solves IMO problems at silver-medal level

title: Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute
description: Showed that spending more compute at inference time, through search and revision, can substitute for a larger model on some tasks.
capabilityNote: Compute-optimal test-time scaling beat a 14x larger model on FLOPs-matched MATH evaluations (reported).

title: Alignment Faking in Large Language Models
description: In an experimental setup, Claude 3 Opus complied with a new training objective when it believed it was being trained, while reasoning about preserving its prior preferences.
capabilityNote: Alignment-faking reasoning appeared in 12% of monitored cases, rising to 78% after RL (per the paper).

title: METR task time horizons
description: Measured the length of software tasks, in human working time, that AI agents complete with 50% reliability. METR later cautioned that its long-horizon measurements are too sparse for exact extrapolation.
capabilityNote: The 50% time horizon doubled roughly every 7 months from 2019 to 2025; later analyses reported faster doubling.

majorUpdates.title: Time-horizon limitations note
majorUpdates.summary: METR noted only 5 of 228 tasks are 16 hours or longer, limiting long-horizon estimates.

sources.title: METR: Measuring AI ability to complete long tasks

title: The Leaderboard Illusion
description: Documented how private testing of many model variants and unequal data access distorted rankings on the Chatbot Arena preference leaderboard. Accepted at NeurIPS 2025.

title: AlphaEvolve
description: An evolutionary coding agent that uses Gemini to propose algorithms and keeps the ones that score best against automated evaluators.
capabilityNote: Found a 48-multiplication algorithm for 4x4 complex matrices and recovered about 0.7% of Google's fleet-wide compute.

title: IMO 2025 gold-medal results
description: General-purpose language models solved olympiad problems in natural language within the contest time limit. DeepMind's result was officially graded; OpenAI announced a self-graded result on Jul 19.
capabilityNote: 35/42 points (5 of 6 problems), gold-medal level.

sources.title: DeepMind: Gemini Deep Think IMO gold

title: ARC-AGI-3
description: The first interactive version of the ARC benchmark, where agents must learn the rules of unfamiliar game-like environments by acting in them.
capabilityNote: In the 30-day preview humans solved 100% of environments; frontier LLMs scored 0–0.37% and the best purpose-built agent 12.58%.

title: ChatGPT
description: A free chat interface to a GPT-3.5 model fine-tuned with RLHF. It put a general-purpose language model in front of the public for the first time at scale.
capabilityNote: About 100M monthly users in roughly 2 months (UBS estimate reported by Reuters, Feb 2023); OpenAI reported 800M weekly users in Oct 2025.

description: An asynchronous coding agent that works on GitHub repositories in a cloud VM; public beta May 20, 2025 and general availability in Aug 2025.

title: Claude Code
description: A terminal coding agent that plans, edits files, and runs commands and tests in the user's repository. It launched as a research preview alongside Claude 3.7 Sonnet.
capabilityNote: Passed a $2.5B annualized revenue run-rate by Feb 2026 (reported).

majorUpdates.title: General availability
majorUpdates.summary: GA alongside Claude Opus 4 and Sonnet 4.

majorUpdates.title: Claude Agent SDK
majorUpdates.summary: The Claude Code harness exposed as a library, renamed from Claude Code SDK.

majorUpdates.title: Agent Skills
majorUpdates.summary: On-demand instruction folders usable in Claude Code.

majorUpdates.title: Claude Code on the web
majorUpdates.summary: Cloud-sandboxed sessions from the browser and iOS.

majorUpdates.title: $2.5B run-rate
majorUpdates.summary: Reported revenue run-rate passed $2.5B.

majorUpdates.title: Dynamic Workflows
majorUpdates.summary: Added orchestrated multi-step workflows (secondary source).

majorUpdates.title: Defaults to Opus 5.5
majorUpdates.summary: Claude Opus 5.5 became the default model (secondary source).

sources.title: Anthropic: Claude 3.7 Sonnet and Claude Code
Anthropic: Claude Code on the web

title: OpenAI Codex (CLI and cloud agent)
description: OpenAI's coding agent, first as an open-source terminal tool (Apr 16, 2025) and then as a cloud agent running tasks in parallel sandboxes (May 16, 2025). Later Codex-specialized GPT models powered it.
capabilityNote: codex-1 reported about 72% SWE-bench Verified.

majorUpdates.title: Codex cloud agent
majorUpdates.summary: Cloud agent on codex-1, an o3 variant.

majorUpdates.title: GPT-5.3-Codex
majorUpdates.summary: Codex-specialized model.

title: Windsurf acquisition saga
description: OpenAI's reported $3B deal for the Windsurf AI editor lapsed; Google paid about $2.4B to license its technology and hire its CEO and staff, and Cognition bought the remaining company.

majorUpdates.title: Windsurf Editor launch
majorUpdates.summary: Agentic IDE with the Cascade agent.

title: Google Antigravity
description: An agent-first IDE launched with Gemini 3, built by the team Google hired in the Windsurf deal. Antigravity 2.0, a CLI and an SDK followed at I/O 2026, drawing on Gemini CLI.

majorUpdates.title: Antigravity 2.0, CLI and SDK
majorUpdates.summary: Announced at Google I/O 2026; a reported Jun 18 Gemini CLI retirement is unconfirmed.

title: SpaceX acquires Cursor
description: SpaceX exercised an option to buy Anysphere, maker of Cursor, in an all-stock deal valued at $60B on Jun 16, 2026; the deal closed Aug 14 and Cursor joined the SpaceXAI team.

title: Midjourney
description: An image generator first offered through Discord and later a web app. Its V5 model produced the photoreal fakes that circulated in 2023, and it added video in 2025.

majorUpdates.title: Open beta
majorUpdates.summary: V2 in April and V3 in July 2022.

majorUpdates.title: V4
majorUpdates.summary: Alpha of a new architecture; niji anime model Dec 20, 2022.

majorUpdates.title: V5
majorUpdates.summary: Photoreal step-change behind viral fakes such as the Pope in a puffer jacket.

majorUpdates.title: V6
majorUpdates.summary: Better prompt following and in-image text; V6.1 Jul 31, 2024.

majorUpdates.title: V7
majorUpdates.summary: New model with Draft mode.

majorUpdates.title: Video V1
majorUpdates.summary: Image-to-video animation, a week after Disney and Universal sued Midjourney.

majorUpdates.title: V8
majorUpdates.summary: V8 alpha; V8.1 Apr 14 and V8.2 Jul 24, 2026.

title: DALL·E 2
description: A diffusion text-to-image model (unCLIP), released through a waitlist and then an open beta on Jul 20, 2022.
capabilityNote: 4x the resolution of DALL·E 1 (OpenAI-reported).

majorUpdates.title: DALL·E 3
majorUpdates.summary: Better prompt adherence using ChatGPT-rewritten captions; in ChatGPT Plus from Oct 2023.

title: Whisper
description: A speech-recognition model trained on 680,000 hours of weakly supervised multilingual audio, with weights released publicly.
capabilityNote: Robust multilingual transcription and translation into English.

title: ElevenLabs
description: Text-to-speech and voice cloning; early misuse to clone public voices led the company to add verification limits.

majorUpdates.title: Eleven v3 alpha
majorUpdates.summary: More expressive speech model.

title: Runway Gen models
description: Runway's video models, from Gen-1 video-to-video style transfer to Gen-2, one of the first commercially available text-to-video models, and later versions with consistent characters.
capabilityNote: Gen-2 produced a few seconds per clip; Gen-3 Alpha 10-second clips.

majorUpdates.title: Gen-2
majorUpdates.summary: Text-to-video.

majorUpdates.title: Gen-3 Alpha
majorUpdates.summary: Higher-fidelity video model.

majorUpdates.title: Gen-4
majorUpdates.summary: Consistent characters and objects across shots; Aleph editing model Jul 2025.

title: Adobe Firefly
description: Adobe's image models, trained on licensed and Adobe Stock content and built into Photoshop as Generative Fill. Adobe's revenue kept growing through the 2026 software selloff.
capabilityNote: Adobe reported a record $6.76B quarter (+13%) for the quarter ended Aug 28, 2026.

majorUpdates.title: Generative Fill in Photoshop
majorUpdates.summary: Firefly editing inside Photoshop.

majorUpdates.title: Premiere and After Effects AI update
majorUpdates.summary: AI masking and motion-design features.

title: Sora (video model)
description: A diffusion-transformer video model previewed with a "world simulators" technical report and released in ChatGPT on Dec 9, 2024.
capabilityNote: Clips up to 60 seconds at preview.

sources.title: OpenAI: Video generation models as world simulators

title: Suno and Udio
description: Music generators that produce full songs with vocals from a prompt. Record labels sued both in Jun 2024; Udio settled with UMG and Suno with Warner Music in late 2025.
capabilityNote: Suno v3 generated songs up to 2 minutes.

majorUpdates.title: Udio launch
majorUpdates.summary: Music-generation app from ex-DeepMind staff.

title: Veo
description: Google's video model line. Veo 3 (May 2025) generated video with synchronized dialogue and sound effects and shipped with the Flow filmmaking tool.
capabilityNote: Veo 3: 8-second clips with native audio.

majorUpdates.title: Veo 2
majorUpdates.summary: Up to 4K output; preferred over Sora Turbo in Google's own evaluations.

majorUpdates.title: Veo 3 and Flow
majorUpdates.summary: Native audio, announced at I/O 2025; Veo 3.1 Oct 15, 2025.

title: Kling
description: A Chinese text-to-video model released publicly before OpenAI opened Sora.
capabilityNote: Up to 2 minutes at 1080p (claimed at launch).

majorUpdates.title: Kling 3.0
majorUpdates.summary: Video, Image 3.0 and Omni models.

title: Genie 3
description: An interactive world model that generates navigable environments in real time, released as a research preview.
capabilityNote: 720p at 24 fps, consistent for a few minutes.

title: Nano Banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image)
description: An image generation and editing model known for keeping characters consistent across edits.
capabilityNote: Drove about 10M first-time Gemini app users (Google, via Wikipedia).

majorUpdates.title: Nano Banana Pro
majorUpdates.summary: Higher-quality variant.

majorUpdates.title: Nano Banana 2
majorUpdates.summary: Second generation; 2 Lite followed Jun 30, 2026.

title: Sora 2 and the Sora app
description: A video model with synchronized audio, launched with a TikTok-style iOS app featuring user "cameos". The app drew copyright-holder backlash, peaked at about 1M users and closed after less than seven months.
capabilityNote: Reached #1 on the US App Store within days (widely reported).

title: OpenAI discontinues Sora
description: OpenAI announced it would close the Sora app and API; the app and website shut on Apr 26, 2026 and the API on Sep 24, 2026. The app reportedly cost about $1M a day to run as users fell below 500,000.

majorUpdates.title: App and web closed
majorUpdates.summary: Consumer Sora app shut down.

majorUpdates.title: API closed
majorUpdates.summary: Sora API shut down.

sources.title: TechCrunch: Why OpenAI really shut down Sora

title: Gemini Omni
description: A model that takes any input and produces any output, starting with video; the Omni Flash version appears in the Gemini app, Flow and YouTube Shorts Remix with SynthID watermarks.

title: NVIDIA H100 (Hopper)
description: A data-center GPU with an FP8 Transformer Engine, announced at GTC 2022 and shipped late that year. It was the main training chip of the 2023–24 buildout.
capabilityNote: Up to 9x faster AI training than A100 (NVIDIA-claimed).

majorUpdates.title: NVIDIA passes $1T
majorUpdates.summary: First chipmaker valued above $1T; reached $5T on Oct 29, 2025.

title: US chip export controls on China
description: Restricted exports of advanced AI chips and chipmaking tools to China; the rules were tightened on Oct 17, 2023.

title: Microsoft's multibillion investment in OpenAI
description: Microsoft extended its partnership with OpenAI in a deal reported at about $10B, with Azure as OpenAI's exclusive cloud.

title: Amazon invests in Anthropic
description: Amazon committed up to $4B, later $8B, making AWS Anthropic's primary cloud with a commitment to its Trainium chips. Google also invested in Oct 2023.

title: NVIDIA Blackwell
description: A two-die GPU with FP4 support, sold as B200 chips and GB200 NVL72 racks; volume shipments ran from late 2024 into 2025.
capabilityNote: 208B transistors; NVL72 racks of 72 GPUs.

title: Google TPUs (v5p to Ironwood)
description: Google's in-house accelerators; Ironwood (v7) was the first TPU designed for inference. Anthropic agreed in Oct 2025 to use up to 1M TPUs.
capabilityNote: Ironwood: 9,216-chip pods at 42.5 exaFLOPS FP8 (Google-claimed).

majorUpdates.title: TPU v5p
majorUpdates.summary: Training TPU announced with Gemini 1.0; 8,960 chips per pod.

majorUpdates.title: Trillium (v6)
majorUpdates.summary: 4.7x peak compute per chip versus v5e (Google-claimed).

title: Stargate Project
description: Announced at the White House as up to $500B for US AI data centers over four years, starting in Abilene, Texas. Oracle signed a $300B compute contract with OpenAI in Sep 2025.

title: DeepSeek market shock
description: After the DeepSeek app topped the US App Store, NVIDIA shares fell about 17%, erasing about $590B, then the largest one-day loss of market value for a US company.
capabilityNote: DeepSeek reported a final V3 training run of about 2.788M H800 GPU-hours (about $5.6M at rental rates, excluding R&D).

sources.title: Reuters: DeepSeek sets off AI market rout

title: Meta Superintelligence Labs formed
description: Meta paid $14.3B for 49% of Scale AI on Jun 12, 2025 and formed Meta Superintelligence Labs on Jun 30, recruiting with large pay packages. The lab's first model was Muse Spark.

title: NVIDIA Vera Rubin
description: NVIDIA's platform after Blackwell; at GTC 2026 it listed seven chips in production, including a Groq 3 inference chip. Systems began shipping to OpenAI, CoreWeave, Google Cloud, Azure and Meta in Jul 2026.
capabilityNote: Jensen Huang projected $1T in Blackwell and Rubin orders through 2027.

title: "Pause Giant AI Experiments" letter
description: An open letter called for a six-month pause on training systems more powerful than GPT-4; no lab paused. A one-sentence statement on extinction risk, signed by lab CEOs, followed in May.

majorUpdates.title: CAIS Statement on AI Risk
majorUpdates.summary: Equated AI extinction risk with pandemics and nuclear war.

title: Geoffrey Hinton leaves Google
description: Hinton resigned from Google so he could speak publicly about the risks of AI.

title: White House voluntary AI commitments
description: Seven AI companies made voluntary commitments to pre-release testing and watermarking.

title: Anthropic Responsible Scaling Policy
description: Defined AI Safety Levels that tie required safeguards to measured model capabilities. ASL-3 protections were first activated for Claude Opus 4 in May 2025.

title: US Executive Order 14110 on AI
description: Required reporting on training runs above 10^26 operations, among other measures. It was revoked on Jan 20, 2025.

title: AI Safety Summit at Bletchley Park
description: 28 countries and the EU signed the Bletchley Declaration and the UK launched its AI Safety Institute. Follow-up summits met in Seoul (May 2024) and Paris (Feb 2025), where the US and UK did not sign the declaration.

title: OpenAI board fires and reinstates Sam Altman
description: The board removed Altman, saying he had not been consistently candid. About 700 of roughly 770 staff threatened to leave, and he was reinstated within five days with a new board.

title: New York Times sues OpenAI and Microsoft
description: A copyright suit over the use of Times articles in training data, one of many suits by authors, image libraries and record labels against AI developers.

sources.title: NYT: Times sues OpenAI and Microsoft

title: License-and-hire deals (Inflection, Character.AI)
description: Microsoft hired Inflection's leadership to run Copilot, and Google licensed Character.AI's technology and rehired its founders (about $2.7B reported). The structure was later used in the Windsurf deal.

majorUpdates.title: Google and Character.AI
majorUpdates.summary: Google licensed the technology and rehired Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas.

title: Sutskever leaves OpenAI, founds Safe Superintelligence
description: Sutskever left OpenAI on May 14, 2024, and the Superalignment team he co-led was dissolved; he founded Safe Superintelligence on Jun 19.

title: EU AI Act enters into force
description: The first comprehensive AI law, with obligations phased in by risk level; prohibitions applied from Feb 2, 2025 and general-purpose model obligations from Aug 2, 2025. In Nov 2025 the Commission proposed delaying some high-risk rules.

majorUpdates.title: Political agreement
majorUpdates.summary: EU institutions reached a deal.

majorUpdates.title: Parliament vote
majorUpdates.summary: European Parliament adopted the Act.

majorUpdates.title: Prohibitions apply
majorUpdates.summary: Banned practices took effect.

majorUpdates.title: GPAI obligations apply
majorUpdates.summary: Rules for general-purpose AI models took effect.

sources.title: European Commission: AI Act enters into force

title: California SB 1047 vetoed
description: California's governor vetoed a frontier-model safety bill; a narrower transparency law, SB 53, was signed on Sep 29, 2025.

title: Nobel Prizes for AI work
description: The Physics prize went to John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton for foundations of neural networks; the next day the Chemistry prize went to Demis Hassabis and John Jumper for AlphaFold and to David Baker for protein design.

title: America's AI Action Plan
description: A deregulatory plan focused on infrastructure and exports, issued after the revocation of Executive Order 14110.

sources.title: White House: America's AI Action Plan

title: Bartz v. Anthropic settlement
description: Anthropic agreed to pay $1.5B, about $3,000 per work, to settle claims over pirated books in its training data, the largest US copyright settlement. The judge had earlier found that training on lawfully acquired books was fair use.

title: OpenAI becomes a public benefit corporation
description: OpenAI recapitalized its for-profit arm as a public benefit corporation, with the OpenAI Foundation holding about 26% and Microsoft about 27%.

title: Commerce directive suspends Mythos and Fable access
description: A US Commerce Department directive barred non-US nationals from Anthropic's Mythos and Fable models; the restriction was lifted on Jun 30 and access restored on Jul 1.

title: Meta Galactica
description: A language model for science that Meta said could summarize papers and write scientific code. Its public demo was withdrawn after three days because it produced confident, false and sometimes offensive text.

title: Humane Ai Pin
description: A screenless wearable assistant pitched as a successor to the phone. About 10,000 units shipped, returns exceeded sales in mid-2024, and HP bought the company's assets for $116M before the pins were disabled on Feb 28, 2025.

majorUpdates.title: Returns exceed sales
majorUpdates.summary: About 7,000 units left in users' hands and roughly $9M in total sales.

majorUpdates.title: HP buys assets
majorUpdates.summary: HP paid $116M; devices bricked Feb 28, 2025.

sources.title: TechCrunch: Humane's AI Pin is dead

title: Rabbit R1
description: A $199 handheld sold on a "Large Action Model" that would operate apps for the user. Reviewers found its launcher ran as an ordinary Android app, and more than 100,000 preorders did not turn into sustained use.

sources.title: Android Authority: Rabbit R1 is an Android app

title: Klarna's AI customer-service assistant
description: Klarna said its OpenAI-based assistant handled two-thirds of customer-service chats in its first month, the work of 700 agents. In May 2025 its CEO said the focus on cost had lowered quality, and Klarna began hiring human agents again.
capabilityNote: 2.3M conversations in the first month (company-reported).

title: Gemini pauses images of people
description: Google paused Gemini's generation of images of people after it produced racially diverse depictions of Nazi-era soldiers and other historical figures. Sundar Pichai told staff the responses were unacceptable.

title: Amazon pulls Just Walk Out from Fresh stores
description: Amazon removed its camera-based checkout from US Fresh grocery stores in favour of smart carts, after reports that more than 1,000 workers in India reviewed transactions. Amazon disputed that humans performed the checkout.

sources.title: NPR: Amazon removes Just Walk Out

title: Google AI Overviews launch errors
description: AI-written summaries at the top of Google Search repeated joke forum posts, including advice to use glue to keep cheese on pizza. Google restricted forum content in answers and kept the feature, and Search revenue grew 17% year on year in Q2 2026.

sources.title: TechCrunch: Google admits AI Overviews need work

title: McDonald's ends IBM AI drive-thru test
description: McDonald's ended its automated voice-ordering pilot in more than 100 restaurants by Jul 26, 2024, after viral order errors, while saying voice ordering would still be part of its future.

sources.title: CNBC: McDonald's to end IBM drive-thru test

title: Friend pendant
description: An always-listening AI companion necklace. After about $1M on New York subway ads in fall 2025, it had sold about 3,000 units and shipped about 1,000 by October, and reviewers reported poor hearing and long lags.
capabilityNote: Under $400K revenue by Oct 2025 (reported).

title: GM ends Cruise robotaxi program
description: GM stopped funding Cruise's robotaxi development after spending more than $10B. Cruise had lost its California permits after an Oct 2023 incident in which a car dragged a pedestrian.

sources.title: CNBC: GM halts Cruise robotaxi funding

title: Builder.ai collapse
description: The Microsoft-backed app-building startup, once valued at about $1.5B, entered insolvency after it emerged it had told creditors of about $220M in 2024 sales against actual revenue near $50M. The core finding was revenue misstatement; claims that its AI was secretly humans are contested.

title: METR developer productivity RCT
description: A randomized trial with 16 experienced open-source developers found tasks took 19% longer with AI tools, though the developers believed they had been 20% faster. METR's 2026 follow-up could not measure cleanly because many developers refused to work without AI.
capabilityNote: −19% measured speed versus +20% self-estimated; follow-up estimate −18% (CI −38% to +9%) for returning developers.

majorUpdates.title: Uplift update
majorUpdates.summary: 57 developers and 800+ tasks; METR said results were likely biased toward slowdown.

sources.title: METR: Early-2025 AI and experienced OS developers

title: Software-stock selloff ("SaaSpocalypse")
description: After Claude Cowork plugins and Claude Opus 4.6, about $285B of software market value fell in roughly 48 hours on fears that agents would replace business applications. Revenues at the largest vendors kept growing through 2026.
capabilityNote: Thomson Reuters fell 15.8% and LegalZoom 19.7%; Salesforce later reported an $11.3B quarter (+11%).

sources.title: The Batch: Cowork plugins trigger SaaS selloff

title: Luma Dream Machine
description: A free public text- and image-to-video app; the Ray2 (Jan 2025) and Ray3 (Sep 2025) models followed.

title: OpenAI acquires io
description: OpenAI bought io, the hardware startup co-founded by former Apple designer Jony Ive, in an all-stock deal of about $6.5B to build AI devices.

title: Salesforce cuts support staff with AI agents
description: Marc Benioff said Salesforce had reduced its support staff from about 9,000 to about 5,000 because AI agents now handled about half of customer interactions. The company said it redeployed hundreds of the affected staff.
capabilityNote: Agentforce ARR above $1.5B by Aug 2026 (company-reported); support costs down 17% (company-reported).

title: Chegg's decline
description: In May 2023 Chegg's CEO called the ChatGPT-driven stock drop overblown. Chegg later cut 22% of staff (May 2025) and 45% (Oct 2025), citing AI and falling Google traffic, and its stock fell about 99% from its peak.

sources.title: CNBC: Chegg CEO on ChatGPT stock plunge
